qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Premium brand equity ('Ultimate Driving Machine') and flexible multi-powertrain manufacturing across BMW, Mini, and Rolls-Royce provide moderate brand loyalty. However, capital efficiency is structurally cyclical and sub-hurdle, with Automotive RoCE falling to 6.6% in 2024 and Group ROIC averaging 7-9% across the cycle (well below the 12% hurdle). Primary erosion threats include aggressive Chinese EV competition (especially in China, ~30% of volume), regulatory fleet emissions mandates, software-defined vehicle execution risks, and customer cross-shopping price elasticity.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & pricing power, REJECT). Premium automotive manufacturing is structurally capital-intensive and cyclical, with Automotive RoCE dropping from a 24% peak in 2021 to 6.6% in 2024 (multi-cycle Group ROIC 7-9% vs 12% hurdle). Faces aggressive Chinese EV price competition, heavy Neue Klasse capex/R&D burdens, and customer cross-shopping elasticity.
qualitative.evidence: Automotive segment RoCE dropped from 24.0% in 2021 and 18.1% in 2022 to 11.3% in 2023 and 6.6% in 2024. Group ROIC over full business cycles hovers around 7-9%, failing the 12% hurdle. Massive ongoing R&D and capex for Neue Klasse electric architecture and software platforms depress returns on incremental capital. China sales (~30% of deliveries) suffer from intense local EV price wars, and vehicle recall disruptions (such as the Continental integrated braking system in 2024) illustrate vulnerability in outsourced critical component supply chains.
